Normative requirement: When placing a product with digital elements on the market, ensure it is designed, developed, and produced in accordance with Annex I Part I.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should use the Annex I Part I register as the product-security baseline for architecture, implementation, default configuration, release readiness, and maintenance planning.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary manufacturer-like readiness scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: Even without formal CE marking, the voluntary readiness scope needs a traceable bridge from product design and development to Annex I Part I properties.
Risk assessment dependency: TokenStream cybersecurity risk assessment should confirm which Annex I Part I requirements apply and how deeply.
Required security capability: Secure-by-design lifecycle; Annex I Part I traceability; architecture and release security review.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §2.6 Cybersecurity Risk Assessment; §3.4 Secure Development Properties; §7.1 Technical File
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: Annex I Part I register; architecture documentation; threat model; release security gate.

Normative requirement: Undertake a cybersecurity risk assessment and use the outcome during planning, design, development, production, delivery, and maintenance to minimise risks, prevent incidents, and minimise impact.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should perform a product cybersecurity risk assessment covering intended use, self-hosted deployment, admin/API surfaces, corpus data, provider/tool integrations, ingestion, retrieval, and update/distribution lifecycle.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary manufacturer-like readiness scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: This is the pivot point after the preliminary requirement register. It converts preliminary applicability into final applicability, implementation depth, and control priorities.
Risk assessment dependency: This requirement is the risk assessment itself; outputs should drive final applicability and required capability depth.
Required security capability: Cybersecurity risk assessment; lifecycle integration; threat scenarios; risk treatment; update cadence.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §2.6 Cybersecurity Risk Assessment; §3.4.9 Threat Model; §7.1.1-§7.1.2 Technical File risk assessment
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: risk assessment report; risk register; threat model; lifecycle review records.

Normative requirement: Document and update the cybersecurity risk assessment as appropriate during the support period.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should version the risk assessment and update it for significant architecture changes, new exposed interfaces, dependency/service changes, major releases, vulnerability discoveries, and support-period changes.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary manufacturer-like readiness scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream evolves through provider integrations, MCP support, ingestion processors, frontend/admin features, and deployment topology changes. Static one-time assessment would not support CRA-style evidence.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define update triggers and review cadence.
Required security capability: Risk assessment governance; change-triggered review; version history; support-period review.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §2.4 Sustainability & Review; §2.6 Cybersecurity Risk Assessment; §7.1 Technical File
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: assessment version history; release review checklist; architecture-change review log.

Normative requirement: Include analysis of cybersecurity risks based on intended purpose, reasonably foreseeable use, conditions of use, operational environment, assets to protect, and expected use time.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream risk assessment should explicitly define intended use, foreseeable misuse, self-hosted operational assumptions, protected assets, trust boundaries, external dependencies, and expected support/use period.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary manufacturer-like readiness scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream sits behind client applications and can be deployed in different environments. The risk picture depends heavily on whether services are exposed publicly, what corpora contain, which providers/tools are enabled, and how operators manage secrets.
Risk assessment dependency: This is core risk assessment content and should be completed before final control design.
Required security capability: Product context; asset inventory; data-flow mapping; trust boundaries; deployment assumptions; foreseeable misuse analysis.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §2.6 Cybersecurity Risk Assessment; §3.4.9 Threat Model; §7.1.1-§7.1.2 Technical File
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: asset register; deployment assumptions; data-flow diagram; misuse cases; support-period rationale.

Normative requirement: Indicate whether and how Annex I Part I 2 requirements apply and are implemented; indicate how Annex I Part I 1 and Annex I Part II vulnerability handling requirements are applied.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should turn the preliminary Annex I Part I and Part II registers into final applicability decisions, implementation rationale, and required security capabilities after the risk assessment.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary manufacturer-like readiness scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: This directly confirms our process: preliminary register first, then risk assessment, then final applicability and capability/control mapping.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment must provide the rationale for final applicability and implementation depth.
Required security capability: Requirement applicability method; traceability; final requirement register; control mapping inputs.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §2.6 Cybersecurity Risk Assessment; §7.1 Technical File; Appendix mapping table
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: finalized requirement register; risk-to-requirement mapping; control library inputs.

Normative requirement: Include the cybersecurity risk assessment in technical documentation and clearly justify any non-applicable essential cybersecurity requirements.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should maintain a technical-file-style evidence package containing the risk assessment and explicit justifications for requirements marked not applicable or conditionally applicable.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable for voluntary technical file; formal obligation conditional on market placement
Preliminary applicability rationale: Although the current target excludes CE marking, a voluntary technical file supports self-certification readiness and prevents weak N/A decisions.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should support each N/A or conditional-applicability rationale.
Required security capability: Technical documentation; N/A rationale; evidence package management; legal-scope marker.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §7.1 Technical File; §2.6 Cybersecurity Risk Assessment
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: technical file index; N/A rationale register; risk assessment attachment.

Normative requirement: Exercise due diligence when integrating third-party components, including non-commercial FOSS, so they do not compromise product cybersecurity.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should assess third-party Python/npm dependencies, container images, base images, external services, optional Open WebUI, Qdrant, MinIO, TEI, and FOSS components before and during integration.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary manufacturer-like readiness scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream depends on many third-party and FOSS components. Component risk can enter through dependency vulnerabilities, unsafe defaults, unmaintained packages, parser libraries, or container images.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should classify critical components and define due diligence depth.
Required security capability: Third-party component due diligence; dependency approval; component risk classification; supply-chain review.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §3.1-§3.3 SBOM & provenance; §3.6 Third-Party Software Supply Chain Qualification; §5.3 Self-Maintained OSS
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: dependency review records; SBOM; container image review; approved component list.

Normative requirement: When identifying a vulnerability in an integrated component, report it to the component manufacturer or maintainer and address/remediate it under Annex I Part II.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should route discovered dependency or bundled-component vulnerabilities upstream where appropriate while also assessing and remediating the impact on TokenStream users.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary manufacturer-like readiness scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: For a FOSS-heavy stack, many vulnerabilities will originate upstream. TokenStream still needs product-context triage, mitigation, and user communication.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define which integrated components are in scope and when upstream reporting is appropriate.
Required security capability: Upstream vulnerability coordination; component vulnerability triage; product-context remediation; advisory linkage.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §4.1 Vulnerability Monitoring; §4.2 Risk Adjudication; §4.4 Disclosure; §5 OSS Stewardship
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: upstream issue/advisory links; vulnerability register; remediation PRs; advisory notes.

Normative requirement: Where the manufacturer develops a software or hardware modification to address an integrated-component vulnerability, share relevant code or documentation with the component maintainer where appropriate, in machine-readable format where appropriate.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should contribute fixes, patches, or technical details upstream when it develops dependency or integration fixes that are useful to component maintainers and safe to disclose.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable where TokenStream develops upstream-relevant fixes
Preliminary applicability rationale: Most TokenStream fixes may be product-level configuration or version bumps, but parser/library/container fixes may produce upstream-relevant patches.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment and disclosure review should determine when sharing is safe, appropriate, and useful.
Required security capability: Upstream contribution process; patch sharing; coordinated disclosure; machine-readable vulnerability/fix information.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §5.1 OSS Contribution & Engagement; §4.4 Disclosure & Regulatory Reporting
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: upstream PRs; patch files; maintainer communication; disclosure timing rationale.

Normative requirement: Systematically document relevant cybersecurity aspects, vulnerabilities known to the manufacturer, relevant third-party information, and update the risk assessment where applicable.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should maintain cybersecurity records covering architecture, security requirements, vulnerabilities, third-party reports, decisions, mitigations, releases, and risk-assessment updates.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary manufacturer-like readiness scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: This is the evidence backbone for the whole process. Without systematic records, later controls and evidence mapping become guesswork.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define what information is relevant and when records trigger reassessment.
Required security capability: Cybersecurity recordkeeping; vulnerability register; decision logs; third-party information tracking; risk assessment update trigger.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §2.4 Sustainability & Review; §4.1-§4.3 Vulnerability Handling; §7.1 Technical File
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: vulnerability register; decision log; third-party advisory archive; risk assessment update history.

Normative requirement: When placing on the market and during the support period, ensure vulnerabilities, including components, are handled effectively according to Annex I Part II.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should define a support-period vulnerability handling process for product code, dependencies, containers, bundled/optional services, and release artifacts.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary manufacturer-like readiness scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: This overlaps with Annex I Part II and gives it a lifecycle boundary. Users need to know when TokenStream vulnerabilities will be monitored and handled.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define support period scope, supported versions, component coverage, and update channels.
Required security capability: Vulnerability handling lifecycle; support-period scope; component monitoring; remediation process.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §4 Vulnerability Handling; §6.1 Support Period & Update Obligations
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: support policy; vulnerability handling policy; release support matrix.

Normative requirement: Determine the support period based on expected use time, user expectations, product nature and intended purpose, relevant law, similar products, operating environment, third-party component support, and proportionality; minimum five years unless expected use is shorter.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should define and publish a support period or rolling-release support model for the OSS distribution, including supported versions/images and end-of-support expectations.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary readiness; formal minimum conditional on market placement
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream is self-hosted software and may be used in long-lived internal systems. Even if the five-year legal minimum is not asserted for current non-commercial OSS, a clear support model is needed.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should inform expected use time, supported deployment assumptions, and whether a shorter or rolling support model is justified.
Required security capability: Support-period determination; version support matrix; end-of-support policy; proportionality rationale.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §6.1 Support Period & Update Obligations; §7.3 User-Facing Docs
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: support period statement; version support matrix; EoS policy; rationale memo.

Normative requirement: Include the information used to determine the support period in technical documentation.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should retain the support-period rationale in the technical-file-style evidence package.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable for voluntary technical file; formal obligation conditional on market placement
Preliminary applicability rationale: The support period must be explainable, not just declared, especially if TokenStream uses a rolling-release model or excludes older unsupported versions.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should feed the expected-use and operational-environment rationale.
Required security capability: Support-period rationale; technical documentation; lifecycle evidence retention.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §6.1 Support Period; §7.1 Technical File
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: support-period rationale memo; technical file index; release lifecycle policy.

Normative requirement: Have appropriate policies and procedures, including CVD policies, to process and remediate potential vulnerabilities reported from internal or external sources.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should maintain a vulnerability handling and CVD process covering reports from maintainers, users, researchers, scanners, dependency feeds, and upstream advisories.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary manufacturer-like readiness scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: The existing SECURITY.md is a starting point, but Article 13 expects enforceable policies and procedures, not only a reporting note.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define severity, escalation, response times, and responsible roles.
Required security capability: Vulnerability intake; CVD policy; triage procedure; internal/external report handling; remediation workflow.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §2.1 CRA Policy; §4.1-§4.4 Vulnerability Handling
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: SECURITY.md; CVD policy; vulnerability runbook; triage records.

Normative requirement: Ensure each security update made available during the support period remains available for at least 10 years after issuance or the remainder of the support period, whichever is longer.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should define retention and availability expectations for security releases, source tags, advisories, container images or digests, and upgrade documentation.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary readiness; formal retention conditional on market placement
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream users may need to access old security releases or advisories to update pinned deployments. Container registry retention and source archive retention require explicit policy.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should identify update channels and artifacts that must remain available.
Required security capability: Security update retention; release archive; advisory retention; artifact availability.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §6.1.2 Security updates; §7.1 Technical File retention
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: release archive policy; GitHub releases/tags; registry retention settings; advisory archive.

Normative requirement: For substantially modified software versions, compliance with Annex I Part II(2) may be ensured only for the latest placed version if previous-version users can access the latest version free of charge and without additional hardware/software adjustment costs.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should decide whether security remediation is maintained for multiple supported versions or only the latest version, and document conditions for free upgrade and compatibility.
Preliminary applicability: Conditional; relevant if version support is limited to latest release
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream likely uses source/container releases where upgrading is free, but environment adjustment costs and breaking changes may still matter for self-hosted operators.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should inform supported-version strategy and upgrade compatibility assumptions.
Required security capability: Version support policy; upgrade compatibility; free upgrade access; substantial modification tracking.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §6.1 Support Period & Update Obligations; §7.2 Downstream Provisioning
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: version support matrix; upgrade guide; breaking-change policy; changelog.

Normative requirement: Public software archives may be maintained, but users must be clearly informed about risks associated with unsupported software.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should label unsupported historical releases, branches, container tags, or documentation versions with clear end-of-support and security-risk notices.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable if historical versions are publicly archived
Preliminary applicability rationale: Open-source projects naturally keep historical Git tags and releases. Users may deploy old versions unless warnings are visible.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should identify unsupported-version risks and necessary warnings.
Required security capability: Unsupported-version warning; archive labeling; EoS communication; release documentation hygiene.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §6.1.4 End-of-support communication; §6.1.6 EoS transition
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: GitHub release notices; docs version warnings; EoS statement; archive policy.

Normative requirement: Before placing on the market, draw up technical documentation referred to in Article 31.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should maintain a voluntary technical-file-style package with product description, architecture, risk assessment, Annex I applicability, security testing, SBOM, vulnerability handling, support period, and user instructions.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable for voluntary readiness; formal obligation conditional on market placement
Preliminary applicability rationale: A technical-file package is useful even without CE marking because it anchors the evidence model and future self-certification readiness.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment determines technical-file content and requirement applicability.
Required security capability: Technical file compilation; evidence index; document ownership; versioning.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §7.1 Technical File
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: technical file index; architecture diagram; risk assessment; SBOM; test reports.

Normative requirement: Carry out or have carried out the chosen conformity assessment procedure under Article 32.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should record that no formal conformity assessment is being performed for the current non-commercial OSS scope; if market-placement scope changes, select and execute the applicable Article 32 route.
Preliminary applicability: Not applicable to current non-commercial OSS objective; legal-scope trigger only
Preliminary applicability rationale: The user has stated there will be no actual CE marking. Keeping this row prevents accidental implied conformity claims.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment may support future conformity assessment, but legal role/scope determines whether this becomes active.
Required security capability: Conformity pathway decision; legal scope review; no-CE disclaimer; future trigger criteria.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §2.5 Product Assessment; §7.3 EU DoC & CE Marking
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: legal/scope memo; no-CE statement; future conformity plan placeholder.

Normative requirement: If conformity is demonstrated, draw up EU Declaration of Conformity and affix CE marking.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should not issue an EU DoC or CE marking in the current non-commercial OSS scope; if scope changes, DoC and CE evidence must follow successful conformity assessment.
Preliminary applicability: Not applicable to current non-commercial OSS objective; legal-scope trigger only
Preliminary applicability rationale: This is deliberately outside the present goal. Including it marks the boundary between readiness evidence and formal market conformity.
Risk assessment dependency: Legal scope and conformity assessment outcome determine applicability.
Required security capability: EU DoC control; CE marking control; conformity evidence release gate.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §7.3 EU DoC & CE Marking; §7.4 EU Declaration of Conformity & CE Marking
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates if future scope changes: DoC, CE marking evidence, conformity assessment records.

Normative requirement: Keep technical documentation and EU DoC available to market surveillance authorities for at least 10 years after market placement or support period, whichever is longer.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should define voluntary evidence retention for the technical-file package; EU DoC retention is not applicable unless a formal DoC is issued later.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable for voluntary technical evidence retention; DoC/MSA obligation conditional on market placement
Preliminary applicability rationale: Retention supports auditability and future transition to formal conformity, while avoiding a false claim that an EU DoC exists.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should inform retention for security-relevant evidence and support-period records.
Required security capability: Evidence retention; technical file archive; access control; DoC retention trigger.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §2.4.4 Record archive; §7.1.5 Technical documentation retention
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: retention policy; archive location; technical file custodian.

Normative requirement: Ensure procedures are in place for series production to remain in conformity and account for changes in development/production, product design/characteristics, harmonised standards, cybersecurity schemes, or common specifications.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should maintain procedures so recurring releases remain aligned with the requirement register, risk assessment, security gates, dependency updates, and evolving standards/guidance.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary release-readiness scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream is software with repeated releases rather than physical series production. The equivalent is release/change governance across code, containers, configs, docs, and standards changes.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define what changes require reassessment or release gate review.
Required security capability: Release governance; change control; standards monitoring; recurrent conformity review; substantial-change trigger.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §2.4 Sustainability & Review; §2.7 Harmonized Standards Tracking; §3.4.10 Release Security Gate
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: release checklist; standards watch log; change impact assessment; CI records.

Normative requirement: Ensure products bear type, batch, serial number, or other identification, or provide that information on packaging/accompanying document where not possible.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should provide unique product and release identification through product name, semantic version, Git tag/commit, container image tag/digest, SBOM metadata, and documentation version.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary readiness scope; physical marking not applicable to software-only distribution
Preliminary applicability rationale: Software-only releases still need clear identity so users can determine affected versions and apply security advisories.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should confirm which artifacts identify deployed product versions.
Required security capability: Product identification; release/version traceability; artifact identity; SBOM product metadata.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §3.1 SBOM Generation; §3.3 Provenance & Integrity; §7.3 User-Facing Docs
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: version.txt; Git tags; image digests; SBOM product fields; release notes.

Normative requirement: Indicate manufacturer name/trade name/trademark, contact address/email/digital contact, website where applicable, and include this in user information; contact details must be understandable to users/MSAs.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should publish maintainer/project identity and security/contact channels in README, documentation, release pages, and user-facing instructions.
Preliminary applicability: Conditional as manufacturer obligation; applicable as voluntary project/contact readiness
Preliminary applicability rationale: The current project is OSS/non-commercial, but users still need to know who maintains the project and how to contact maintainers for security and support questions.
Risk assessment dependency: Legal scope should determine whether "manufacturer" identity is declared; risk assessment does not decide legal identity.
Required security capability: Project identity; contact publication; user documentation; legal-role marker.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §7.3 User-Facing Documentation; §5.2 Steward vs Maintainer Boundaries
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: README contact section; SECURITY.md; project website; maintainer/legal role memo.

Normative requirement: Designate a single point of contact for direct and rapid communication, including vulnerability reporting; make it easily identifiable, include it in user instructions, and do not limit communication to automated tools.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should provide a clear human-reachable security contact and vulnerability reporting path, not only automated issue templates or bots.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary readiness scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: The current SECURITY.md says report privately to the maintainer, but a CRA-ready register should capture a concrete contact and communication process.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define severity escalation, but contact designation is a governance decision.
Required security capability: Single point of contact; vulnerability reporting channel; non-automated communication path; user instruction update.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §4.4 Disclosure & Regulatory Reporting; §7.3 User-Facing Documentation
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: SECURITY.md contact; security.txt; docs contact page; response runbook.

Normative requirement: Ensure the product is accompanied by Annex II information and user instructions in understandable language, clear and legible, enabling secure installation, operation, and use; keep online/user info available for 10 years or support period if longer.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should provide user/operator documentation covering intended use, secure installation, configuration, secrets, exposed ports, update installation, vulnerability reporting, support period, secure decommissioning, and integrator guidance.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary readiness scope; formal retention conditional on market placement
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream is self-hosted and security depends heavily on operator configuration. Clear secure-use instructions are a real security requirement even outside CE marking.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should identify security-relevant instructions, foreseeable misuse, and operator assumptions.
Required security capability: Secure user documentation; Annex II checklist; operations guide; documentation retention; language/accessibility decision.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §7.3 User-Facing Documentation; §7.2 Downstream Customer Provisioning
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: README; quickstart; operations guide; Annex II mapping; secure deployment guide.

Normative requirement: Ensure the support-period end date, at least month and year, is clearly specified at purchase/access time and where applicable by digital means; where technically feasible, notify users when support ends.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should publish support-period or supported-version information in release/docs channels and warn users about unsupported versions where technically feasible.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary readiness scope; purchase-time language conditional on market placement
Preliminary applicability rationale: Self-hosted OSS users often access the project through GitHub/docs rather than purchase. The equivalent is a visible support/version policy and EoS notices.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should inform expected use time and support strategy.
Required security capability: Support-period communication; EoS notification; supported-version policy; unsupported-version warnings.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §6.1.1 Support Period; §6.1.4 End-of-support communication
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: support policy; release page notices; docs banner; EoS announcement template.

Normative requirement: Provide EU Declaration of Conformity or simplified EU Declaration of Conformity with exact URL for full DoC.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should not provide an EU DoC in the current no-CE non-commercial OSS scope; if scope changes, maintain DoC publication/access process.
Preliminary applicability: Not applicable to current non-commercial OSS objective; legal-scope trigger only
Preliminary applicability rationale: This is a formal market conformity artifact and outside the stated certification-readiness goal.
Risk assessment dependency: Legal scope and conformity assessment determine applicability, not cybersecurity risk alone.
Required security capability: DoC publication trigger; no-DoC disclaimer; future conformity artifact management.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §7.3 EU DoC & CE Marking; §7.4 EU Declaration of Conformity & CE Marking
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates if future scope changes: simplified DoC, full DoC URL, DoC version history.

Normative requirement: From market placement and during support period, if manufacturer knows or has reason to believe product or processes are non-conformant with Annex I, immediately take corrective measures to restore conformity or withdraw/recall as appropriate.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should define a corrective-action process for discovered security nonconformities, including emergency fixes, mitigations, advisories, disabling unsafe features, or withdrawing affected releases where appropriate.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary readiness; withdrawal/recall formalism conditional on market placement
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream can discover serious gaps in controls, vulnerability handling, secure defaults, or released artifacts. A corrective-action process is useful even if formal recall is out of scope.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define severity thresholds and corrective action urgency.
Required security capability: Corrective action; nonconformity triage; emergency release; release withdrawal; user notification.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §4.3 Actionable Decisions; §4.4 Disclosure; §6.1 Update Obligations
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: corrective action log; emergency release runbook; advisory; withdrawn tag/image record if needed.

Normative requirement: Provide information and documentation to market surveillance authority on reasoned request and cooperate on measures to eliminate cybersecurity risks.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should maintain a voluntary response workflow for technical-file/evidence requests; formal MSA cooperation applies only if CRA market scope is triggered.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable for voluntary evidence readiness; formal MSA obligation conditional on market placement
Preliminary applicability rationale: A response workflow ensures evidence is locatable and helps avoid panic if future legal scope changes. It should not imply current market surveillance obligations.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should inform what evidence must be available; legal role determines formal MSA obligation.
Required security capability: Evidence request workflow; document retrieval; cooperation procedure; legal escalation.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §7.1.3 MSA deliverables; §7.1.6 MSA response workflow
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: evidence index; response SOP; named custodian; legal escalation path.

Normative requirement: If the manufacturer ceases operations and cannot comply, inform relevant market surveillance authorities and users of affected products before cessation.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should define project discontinuation or maintainer-exit communication for users, including security support implications and archived status; formal authority notification is conditional on market placement.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable as voluntary project continuity/EoS readiness; formal MSA obligation conditional
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream users could be harmed by silent abandonment because vulnerabilities and dependencies continue to evolve. OSS project continuity should be explicit.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should inform user impact and transition needs if support ceases.
Required security capability: Cessation communication; project archival policy; EoS transition; user notification.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §6.1.5-§6.1.6 EoS transition; §2.4 Sustainability & Review
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: project archival procedure; EoS announcement template; maintainer succession note.

Normative requirement: The Commission may specify SBOM format and elements by implementing acts, taking into account standards and best practices.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should monitor CRA implementing acts, harmonised standards, common specifications, and SBOM format guidance, and update its SBOM profile accordingly.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable as standards-monitoring readiness
Preliminary applicability rationale: SBOM expectations may evolve. A static SBOM profile may become stale before formal CRA deadlines or future distribution changes.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should identify SBOM use cases, but standards monitoring determines format updates.
Required security capability: Regulatory/standards monitoring; SBOM profile maintenance; tooling update process.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §2.7 Harmonized Standards Tracking; §3.1 SBOM Generation; §3.2 SBOM Data Quality
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: standards watch log; SBOM profile; tooling validation reports.

Normative requirement: ADCO may conduct dependency assessments for product categories and market surveillance authorities may request relevant SBOMs for anonymised/aggregated dependency information.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should be able to produce relevant SBOMs for dependency-analysis requests if future market scope applies; voluntary readiness should ensure SBOMs are retrievable and product-version specific.
Preliminary applicability: Conditional on market scope and authority request; voluntary SBOM readiness applicable
Preliminary applicability rationale: This is not a day-to-day product control, but it reinforces the need for accurate, retrievable SBOMs tied to released versions.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should classify component criticality, but legal/authority request triggers formal response.
Required security capability: SBOM retrieval; dependency assessment support; release-to-SBOM traceability; authority request workflow.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §3.1-§3.2 SBOM; §7.1 Technical File; §7.2 SBOM provisioning
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: release SBOM archive; SBOM-to-version mapping; response workflow.
